result.summary: Besieged at Eira, the Messenians raid Laconia, and the Spartans halt farming there, which brings scarcity and riots at home. Aristomenes raids Amyclæ but is captured and thrown into the Ceadas pit, from which he escapes by following a fox.

scenes.title: Messenian raids and Spartan scarcity
scenes.summary: Aristomenes and his picked men plunder Laconia and Messenia. The Spartans stop farming, and scarcity and riots follow.
scenes.stakes: The Spartans risk famine and unrest at home; the Messenians risk reprisal.

scenes.title: Raid on Amyclæ and capture
scenes.summary: Aristomenes surprises Amyclæ at night, then is wounded and captured with fifty men. They are thrown into the Ceadas, and the others die.
scenes.stakes: Aristomenes faces death by being thrown into the Ceadas.

scenes.title: Escape from Ceadas
scenes.summary: In the pit Aristomenes seizes a fox and follows it to a small hole, which he enlarges to escape home to Eira.
scenes.stakes: He faces death by starvation in the pit.

characters.name: Tyrtæus
characters.description: Poet whose verses calmed Spartan unrest

notable_quotes.reason: Vivid account of Aristomenes using the fox to find a way out.

analysis.text: Aristomenes' courage and the sense of divine favour make him a near-legendary hero of Messenian resistance.
Pausanias distinguishes reported marvels like the eagle from plausible events, showing his rationalizing approach to legend.

fun_facts.text: The Ceadas was a chasm near Sparta used for executing criminals.

language_notes.text: Eira was the mountain stronghold where the Messenians made their last stand in the Second Messenian War against Sparta.
Lacedæmonians is the Spartans' other name, from Lacedaemon, the region of Laconia.
Tyrtæus was the poet whose war-songs encouraged the Spartans in this war; his verses calmed their discontent.
"Stole a march upon" means gained an advantage by moving secretly and earlier than the enemy expected.
"Genius" here means a guardian spirit (Latin genius) assigned to a person, not intelligence.

context_notes.text: Pylos and Mothone were coastal towns that still held out as Messenian.
Amyclæ was an old town a few miles from Sparta, famous for its shrine of Apollo.
The Ceadas was a chasm near Sparta used to execute criminals by throwing them in.

literary_notes.text: Aristomenes is presented as favoured by fate, building his heroic image through the contrast with the others' deaths.
The eagle legend is a deliberate exaggeration, which Pausanias attributes to admirers and distances himself from.
The brisk, plain telling of the dragging run makes the escape feel vivid and immediate.
The closing remark on his divine help and good fortune sums up the theme of the hero's providential survival.
